messages:
jamie: heads up — after rolling the multi-variant routing change to canary, we're seeing p50 throughput drop ~18% on short-seq chat workloads. suspect batch formation / compat fragmentation. anyone seen this?
sasha: saw something similar on the perf dashboard earlier this morning. mean batch_size fell from ~4.1 -> ~2.6, token_budget target not being hit. :thinking:
lee: KV hit rate looks stable across the canary pool, so not purely cache miss. profiler shows more kernel switches per request — looks like incompat sets are splitting batches.
maria: posted a quick flamegraph: https://go/reports/flame-1791239876 (private). top shows scheduler + coalescer overhead increased. attaching pseudo snippet of the coalescer loop: ```py
# queue sampler (simplified)
while queue.not_empty():
    compatset = pick_compat(queue.head)
    batch = coalesce(queue, compatset, token_budget)
    dispatch(batch)
```
jamie: what changed in compat selection? we only loosened routing rules, shouldn't cause more fragmentation...
sasha: the canary also expanded quantization-profile checks when we added variant metadata. paradoxically that makes the compat match stricter: small differences in qprofile => separate buckets.
lee: also observed more frequent fallback hops — when capacity spiky, requests fall back to smaller variants which then interleave with the newer variant requests. that interleaving prevents the coalescer from forming homogeneous batches.
vika: quick profiler numbers: kernel_switches/request +30%, avg_batch_size from 3.4 -> 2.1 on canary, scheduling latency +~6ms p50. KV warmups: a subset of fallbacks cause KV fingerprint mismatch => rebuilds (~2-3ms each).
maria: KV rebuilds show in traces as: `kv: rebuild(key=... variant=v2) duration=2.7ms` repeatedly for the same session when variant flips.
jamie: initial hypothesis: two levers — token_budget and compat matching strictness. If we raise token_budget the coalescer will wait longer and likely form larger batches for short sequences. Also consider relaxing quant-profile equality in compat sets (tolerant match).
sasha: I ran a small dev experiment: token_budget 64 -> 128 for the short-chat route. avg_batch_size went up to ~3.5 and p50 throughput recovered. downside: p99 latency for long-seq workloads increased slightly (~18ms). tradeoff.
lee: suggests dynamic token_budget based on per-route seq-length quantiles. e.g., short-chat gets more wait, long-text keeps low wait. I can spin up a simulator to try adaptive policy.
maria: alternative: postpone kernel selection until batch closure. right now we pick kernel per-request which forces early decisions and sometimes causes a batch to split when a later request would require a different kernel. delaying could let us coalesce requests and then pick a single kernel for the batch. microbench I ran shows fewer kernel switches.
vika: ran a micro A/B: delaying kernel select until batch close reduced kernel_switches/request by ~60% and lowered tail latency by ~12% in the microbench. needs integration testing (KV interactions + memory pinning).
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary rollback window 2026-03-18T03:00Z
jamie: good. action items: 1) revert strict quant-match in compat set to tolerant mode (short-term), 2) experiment with dynamic token_budget per route (simulator + canary), 3) delay kernel selection until batch closure (prototype -> canary), 4) add a KV-compatible variant fingerprint to avoid rebuilds on near-identical variants. volunteers?
sasha: I'll take (1) and (4) — will open a PR tomorrow with tests.
lee: I'll own (2) and run the simulator for mixed-variant traffic. will try simple rule: token_budget = clamp( base * (1 + short_seq_frac), min, max ).
maria: I'll prototype (3) delaying kernel selection; have a microbench harness ready to run against canary.
jamie: please drop short perf numbers and flamegraph links in this thread as you get them. also add any regression dashboards you update. :thumbsup:
sasha: note for the PR: config toggle names I propose -> `compat.tolerance_mode = "tolerant"` and `coalescer.token_budget_override[route]` so we can A/B by route. example config snippet: ```yaml
coalescer:
  default_token_budget: 64
  per_route_overrides:
    "/chat/short": 128
compat:
  tolerance_mode: tolerant # tolerant | strict
```
lee: simulator plan: feed mixed-variant arrival traces (proportion 70/30 new/old), vary seq-length mix, measure mean batch size, kernel_switches, p50/p99 latencies. will post results.
vika: thumbs up. I'll also add a trace filter to highlight KV rebuilds so we can correlate variant flips -> rebuilds.
jamie: thanks all. let's aim to have first numbers in the next 12 hours and decide whether to flip canary back or roll forward with compatible-mode.
